draft.briefing: Hey, you're at Point Calimere! This low headland, also called Kodiakkarai, is where the Coromandel Coast takes an almost right-angle turn. Sri Lanka is just 48 km to the south, and the sanctuary here gets big flocks of greater flamingos.
draft.hungryLine: Kodiakkarai is a quiet stretch of coast, so stock up on food and water in Vedaranyam, about 9 km north.

moodReplies.show-me-around: Point Calimere Wildlife and Bird Sanctuary is a 17 min walk away, home to blackbuck and flocks of waterbirds. Look for Ramarpatham, the highest point of the cape, too.
moodReplies.somewhere-to-chill: Find a spot by the water where the Palk Strait meets the Bay of Bengal and watch the waterbirds come and go.
moodReplies.surprise-me: The highest point of the whole cape, Ramarpatham, is only 4 metres above sea level.

legends.title: Rama's feet
legends.body: A stone slab on the cape carries the impressions of two feet. Locals say this is where Rama stood to scout out Ravana's kingdom in Sri Lanka.

tips.title: Come early for the birds.
tips.body: The sanctuary is known for big gatherings of waterbirds, and mornings are the calmest time to watch them.

tips.title: Read Ponniyin Selvan.
tips.body: Kalki mentions Kodiakkarai in his historical novel, so it's a fun read before you come.

story.title: Temple and lighthouse
story.body: The Cholas built the Kodi Kuzhagar temple here, along with a lighthouse. Both show how old this corner of the coast is.

story.title: A sanctuary for blackbuck
story.body: Point Calimere Wildlife and Bird Sanctuary was created to protect the blackbuck. It covers about 21 square km where the Palk Strait meets the Bay of Bengal.

story.title: Ramsar site
story.body: Kodiakkarai was named a Ramsar wetland in August 2002. It's also listed as an Important Bird Area.

story.title: The tsunami
story.body: The Indian Ocean tsunami destroyed the old Chola lighthouse. The cape and its wetlands still draw flamingos and other waterbirds today.
